correctness.rationale: The concatenation identity represents every continuation after a given input prefix as F_{q,s,t}; different triples are inequivalent since Rudin–Shapiro is not ultimately periodic and a nonzero translation difference cannot be two-periodic. An exact level bound B+3 follows from the two quotient classes and from the opposite values at 4j+2, 4j+3. Dyadic levels give one, two, three, four per level and four final zero-quotient states, yielding 4m+2. Independently built carry automata were minimized for 2,048 offsets and matched the residual formula; finite tests supplement rather than replace the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: Minimal DFAO state complexity of natural translated automatic sequences is an actively studied exact invariant, and the 2025 motivating paper highlights input orientation and shifted-state questions. The theorem gives a complete arbitrary-offset exact computation by O(log c) small interval tests, rigorously proves no residual mergers, and derives the nontrivial dyadic count 4m+2. This is substantially more informative than generic closure or the previously known O(log c) shift-automaton construction and is not merely a particular arbitrary finite parameter census.
